title: US Depository Institutions Deregulation and Monetary Control Act
summary: Deregulated interest-rate ceilings on deposits (Regulation Q), allowed S&Ls to offer adjustable-rate mortgages, and removed many portfolio restrictions — unleashing rate competition that S&Ls, locked into fixed-rate loans, could not survive.

title: US S&L crisis escalates
summary: Around 1,000 savings and loan associations failed between 1986 and 1995. Deposit insurance (FSLIC) covered losses; the eventual taxpayer cost exceeded $130bn. Root cause: maturity mismatch — long fixed-rate mortgages funded by short deposits in a high-rate environment — compounded by regulatory forbearance and moral hazard.

title: Norwegian banking crisis begins
summary: Following rapid credit expansion after financial deregulation in 1984–85, Norwegian banks accumulated large property and shipping loan losses. Christiania Bank and Fokus Bank required state capital injections by 1991; Den norske Bank followed. The government ultimately took full ownership of the three largest banks, wiping out shareholders entirely.

title: Swedish banking crisis: Första Sparbanken collapses
summary: Sweden's credit boom of the late 1980s ended abruptly when the Riksbank defended the krona peg with overnight rates above 500%. Real estate prices collapsed; non-performing loans swelled to 11% of GDP by 1993. The government issued a blanket guarantee of all bank liabilities and created 'bad banks' (Securum, Retriva) to manage distressed assets — a template for subsequent crisis management.

title: Finnish banking crisis — worst of the Nordic trio
summary: Finland's banking losses peaked at 13% of GDP — the largest bank losses of any OECD country to that point. The collapse of the Soviet export market, a fixed exchange-rate regime, and a post-deregulation credit bubble combined. The government recapitalised STS Bank and KOP; Skopbank required central-bank emergency support as early as 1991.

title: BNP Paribas suspends redemptions on three ABS funds
summary: BNP Paribas suspended withdrawals from three funds exposed to US subprime MBS, citing inability to value assets. This froze the European ABCP market overnight, triggering a global liquidity scramble. The ECB injected €95bn in emergency liquidity the same day — the first large-scale crisis intervention. Widely regarded as the start of the 2007–09 crisis.

title: Northern Rock: first UK bank run in 140 years
summary: Northern Rock, a UK mortgage lender almost entirely dependent on wholesale funding, suffered the first visible retail bank run since Overend & Gurney (1866) after the Bank of England's LOLR support became public. Queues formed outside branches. Nationalised in February 2008; the episode exposed the gap between deposit insurance design and depositor behaviour under stress.

title: Bear Stearns acquired by JPMorgan with Fed support
summary: Bear Stearns, the fifth-largest US investment bank, faced a run on its repo funding as counterparties refused to roll overnight positions. The Federal Reserve provided an emergency $29bn non-recourse loan to facilitate a JPMorgan acquisition at $2/share (later raised to $10). The Fed invoked its emergency lending authority under Section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act for the first time since the 1930s.

title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
summary: Lehman's $613bn bankruptcy — the largest in US history — triggered global money-market panic, froze interbank lending, and exposed the fragility of the shadow-banking system that had financed the housing boom. The Reserve Primary Fund 'broke the buck' the following day after writing off Lehman commercial paper, triggering a run on money-market funds.

title: AIG rescued by US government for $85bn
summary: AIG's Financial Products division had sold CDS protection on roughly $440bn of structured credit products. As collateral calls mounted, AIG faced insolvency. The Fed provided an $85bn revolving credit facility in exchange for a 79.9% equity stake — a de facto nationalisation. The rescue prevented a cascade of CDS losses across global banks that AIG had 'insured'.

title: Fed extends unlimited dollar swap lines to major central banks
summary: The Fed removed size limits on dollar swap lines with the ECB, Bank of England, Bank of Japan, and Swiss National Bank, providing unlimited dollar liquidity to non-US banks facing acute dollar funding stress. The FX swap basis had blown out to –200bp, signalling extreme dollar scarcity. Swap-line availability collapsed the basis and restored dollar funding markets within weeks.

title: Greece requests EU/IMF bailout — Eurozone sovereign crisis begins
summary: Greece's admission that its deficit was 12.7% of GDP (not 3.7% as reported) triggered a reassessment of peripheral sovereign creditworthiness. Spreads on Greek, Irish, Portuguese, and Spanish debt surged. The crisis exposed the 'doom loop' between weak sovereigns and their domestic banks — each held large quantities of the other's debt.
